passages:
Generic conformances own their telescopes independently of data declarations.
Select one through a nested application with every type, const,
and static-machine argument explicit; expected shape or visibility cannot infer
them. Lifetime elision is application-only, under the rule below. Proof-only
and runtime-capable implementations use the same conformance model. Their
requirements determine execution and erasure; absence of a data subject is
universal and does not exclude an implementation from dynamic selection.

An inline member is an ordinary machine with its own identity and supplies
one exact requirement overload. When inherited names or overloads collide,
its signature and ordinary exact `satisfies Trait<...>::member` edge identify
the requirement; ambiguity rejects rather than selecting by visibility.
Member implementations refine the requirement's complete
[machine contract](machines.md#substitution), not merely its value signature.
A forwarding body must meet those same proof, ownership and operational
obligations. Forwarding does not equate the member with its callee, donate the
callee's establishment authority, or erase trust dependencies. Optimizations
may eliminate a call or share physical code only while preserving these
semantic identities and contracts; correctness never depends on that optimization.

Type parameters use ordinary angle-bracket applications. `const N: u64` binds
a static value of the declared carrier, usable in layouts, ranges, and contracts.
`N: u64` binds a value which may be known statically or supplied at runtime.
Every application validates the complete argument tuple, including kinds,
ranges, and constraints of unused parameters. Conflicting, excessive, or
incomplete selections reject.

passages:
Constants are not fields and do not contribute to `size_of<T>()`. Their complete
types recursively permit copying and have no cleanup obligation, shared
ownership, or interior mutability. Fixed arrays, records, and copy-eligible sums
are eligible; selecting an unrestricted active case does not make a structurally
linear sum eligible. A constant has no stable address and grants no authority.

A constant position requests semantic evaluation. An initializer may call an
ordinary machine only when that concrete invocation is admitted for evaluation;
there is no separate `const machine` species. The evaluator's admission contract
is described in [semantic evaluation](evaluation.md#invocation-admission).
Effectful [build execution](../build/execution.md) is a separate operation.

passages:
For an eligible runtime-capable machine, evaluation produces exactly the value
that target execution would produce with the same arguments, selected
conformances/providers, and target semantics. Evaluation changes when, not what.
Proof-only machines need no runtime representation but obey the same core value
semantics and cannot observe the compiler phase.
